root_cause.text: `rtm_get_nexthop()` in `net/ipv4/nexthop.c` used a fixed `NLMSG_GOODSIZE` skb allocation for `RTM_GETNEXTHOP` replies, but nexthop group netlink serialization can exceed that size, causing an undersized buffer and `WARN_ON`/message-building failure for large nexthop groups.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `alloc_skb(NLMSG_GOODSIZE, GFP_KERNEL)` with `nlmsg_new(nh_nlmsg_size(nh, op_flags), GFP_KERNEL)` in `rtm_get_nexthop()`, and the CVE description says the fixed allocation “fails for large nexthop groups like 512 nexthops” and triggers a warning at `rtm_get_nexthop+0x176`; it also updates `nh_nlmsg_size_grp()` to account for `op_flags` and missing `NHA_FDB` size, confirming the reply size calculation was incomplete.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend nexthop group netlink size calculation to include FDB and optional stats-related attributes.
intent_record.what: The function `nh_nlmsg_size_grp()` was changed to take an extra `u32 op_flags` argument, its base netlink message size now also accounts for `NHA_FDB`, and it conditionally adds additional size for group statistics, per-entry statistics, hardware statistics, and `NHA_HW_STATS_USED` when `NHA_OP_FLAG_DUMP_STATS` and `NHA_OP_FLAG_DUMP_HW_STATS` are set.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the size calculation for nexthop group netlink messages now includes space for optional FDB and statistics attributes, preventing under-allocation when dumping group stats or hardware stats and enabling those attributes to be emitted safely.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass operation flags into nexthop netlink size calculation so group message sizing matches the attributes that will be emitted.
intent_record.what: The function `nh_nlmsg_size` was changed to take an additional `u32 op_flags` parameter, and its call to `nh_nlmsg_size_grp` was updated to pass `op_flags` along. The rest of the size calculation logic shown in the hunk is unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the nexthop netlink message size computation can now account for operation-specific flags when sizing group nexthop messages. This allows the group size calculation to be context-aware instead of using only the nexthop object state, which can prevent mismatches between computed message size and the actual attributes that will be emitted.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update nexthop netlink notification allocation to use the revised message size calculation.
intent_record.what: The call to nlmsg_new() in nexthop_notify() was changed from nlmsg_new(nh_nlmsg_size(nh), gfp_any()) to nlmsg_new(nh_nlmsg_size(nh, 0), gfp_any()).
intent_record.how: This changes the size calculation used when allocating the netlink message skb, passing an explicit zero value to nh_nlmsg_size(). At runtime, the notification message buffer will be sized according to the updated sizing logic, which may account for the new parameter and prevent mis-sized allocations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Delay nexthop reply allocation until after lookup and allocate the exact required netlink message size.
intent_record.what: The function `rtm_get_nexthop()` was changed to look up the nexthop entry before allocating the reply skb. The fixed-size `alloc_skb(NLMSG_GOODSIZE, GFP_KERNEL)` allocation was removed and replaced with `nlmsg_new(nh_nlmsg_size(nh, op_flags), GFP_KERNEL)` after `nexthop_find_by_id(net, id)` succeeds. The failure path for a missing nexthop now jumps to `out` instead of `errout_free`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now only allocates netlink reply buffer space after confirming the nexthop exists, and it allocates exactly as much space as the specific nexthop message needs. This avoids wasting memory on a generic buffer size, and it prevents attempting to size the reply before the object being reported is known. Missing nexthops still return `-ENOENT`, and allocation failure still returns `-ENOBUFS`.

consistency_review.core_intent: Align nexthop netlink message sizing and allocation with the actual attributes emitted, including deferring reply allocation until after lookup.

relevance_review.reason: The root cause is an undersized skb allocation during nexthop netlink reply size calculation. This group directly changes nexthop group netlink size accounting, which is the same area and addresses size underestimation for serialized nexthop groups.

The changes directly address the root cause: they fix nexthop netlink message sizing/allocation to match the attributes actually serialized, and they defer reply allocation until after lookup instead of using a fixed undersized buffer.

candidates.rationale: This fixed-size skb allocation is the direct root cause: RTM_GETNEXTHOP replies for large nexthop groups can exceed NLMSG_GOODSIZE, leaving too little space for serialization and triggering WARN_ON/message-building failure.

vuln_statements.explanation: This fixed-size skb allocation is the root cause: RTM_GETNEXTHOP replies for large nexthop groups can require more than NLMSG_GOODSIZE, so this statement can create an undersized buffer and lead to WARN_ON/message-building failure during netlink serialization.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in `rtm_get_nexthop()`: it allocates a fixed-size reply buffer with `skb = alloc_skb(NLMSG_GOODSIZE, GFP_KERNEL);` and then serializes the nexthop into it via `nh_fill_node(...)`. The root cause says RTM_GETNEXTHOP replies could exceed this fixed size for large nexthop groups; this code has no dynamic sizing or preflight size calculation. There is no corrective handling here (no larger allocation, no retry, no size check against nexthop-group serialization), so the fix is not present.
